ucs.title: [LLM] LockBit (BITWISE SPIDER) pre-encryption recovery inhibition chain — vssadmin + bcdedit + wbadmin in one window
ucs.description: Hunts the LockBit 3.0/Black encryptor's built-in pre-encryption routine, which natively shells out to delete volume shadow copies, disable Windows boot recovery via bcdedit, and wipe the backup catalog before mass file encryption. Catches LockBit specifically because its binary issues this exact multi-tool combination automatically rather than as discrete operator commands.
ucs.splunk:
| tstats `security_content_summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("vssadmin.exe","wmic.exe","bcdedit.exe","wbadmin.exe","powershell.exe","cmd.exe")) AND (Processes.process="*delete*shadows*" OR Processes.process="*shadowcopy*delete*" OR Processes.process="*resize*shadowstorage*" OR Processes.process="*recoveryenabled*no*" OR Processes.process="*bootstatuspolicy*ignoreallfailures*" OR Processes.process="*delete*catalog*" OR Processes.process="*delete*systemstatebackup*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process span=10m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| stats values(process) as commands values(process_name) as recovery_tools dc(process_name) as distinct_recovery_tools min(firstTime) as firstTime max(lastTime) as lastTime by dest user
| where distinct_recovery_tools >= 2
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
ucs.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("vssadmin.exe","wmic.exe","bcdedit.exe","wbadmin.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("delete shadows","shadowcopy delete","resize shadowstorage","recoveryenabled no","bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures","delete catalog","delete systemstatebackup","Disable-ComputerRestore")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Commands=make_set(ProcessCommandLine, 20), RecoveryTools=make_set(FileName), DistinctRecoveryTools=dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, AccountName
| where DistinctRecoveryTools >= 2   // >=2 distinct recovery-inhibition binaries in window = LockBit-style automated chain, not a lone admin vssadmin
| order by LastSeen desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has_any ("vssadmin.exe","wmic.exe","bcdedit.exe","wbadmin.exe","powershell.exe","cmd.exe")
| where CommandLine has_any ("delete shadows","shadowcopy delete","resize shadowstorage","recoveryenabled no","bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures","delete catalog","delete systemstatebackup","Disable-ComputerRestore")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Commands=make_set(CommandLine, 20), RecoveryTools=make_set(NewProcessName), DistinctRecoveryTools=dcount(NewProcessName) by Computer, SubjectUserName
| where DistinctRecoveryTools >= 2
| order by LastSeen desc
ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: LockBit Recovery Inhibition Command Execution
id: 7c3f1a2e-9b4d-4f1a-8c2e-1d3f4a5b6c7d
status: experimental
description: Detects a single recovery-inhibition command of the kind LockBit's encryptor issues before mass encryption (shadow copy deletion, bcdedit recovery tamper, backup catalog wipe).
references:
  - https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa23-165a
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_img:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\vssadmin.exe'
      - '\wmic.exe'
      - '\bcdedit.exe'
      - '\wbadmin.exe'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'delete shadows'
      - 'shadowcopy delete'
      - 'resize shadowstorage'
      - 'recoveryenabled no'
      - 'bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures'
      - 'delete catalog'
      - 'delete systemstatebackup'
  condition: selection_img and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate backup software maintenance windows
level: high
tags:
  - attack.impact
  - attack.t1490
  - attack.t1486
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\vssadmin.exe OR *\VSSADMIN.EXE OR *\wmic.exe OR *\WMIC.EXE OR *\bcdedit.exe OR *\BCDEDIT.EXE OR *\wbadmin.exe OR *\WBADMIN.EXE) @CommandLine:(*delete*shadows* OR *shadowcopy*delete* OR *recoveryenabled*no* OR *bootstatuspolicy*ignoreallfailures* OR *delete*catalog* OR *delete*systemstatebackup*)
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\(vssadmin|wmic|bcdedit|wbadmin)\.exe$/i
| regex("(?i)(delete\s+shadows|shadowcopy\s+delete|resize\s+shadowstorage|recoveryenabled\s+no|bootstatuspolicy\s+ignoreallfailures|delete\s+catalog|delete\s+systemstatebackup)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName], function=[count(field=ImageFileName, distinct=true, as=distinct_tools), collect([CommandLine]), min(_time, as=firstTime), max(_time, as=lastTime)])
| distinct_tools >= 2
ucs.rationale: LockBit's encryptor (2.0/3.0/Black) does not rely on the operator to wipe recovery options — it spawns vssadmin, wmic, bcdedit and wbadmin itself in rapid succession right before encryption. Requiring >=2 distinct recovery-inhibition binaries in one short window cuts the lone-admin-vssadmin false positives and isolates the automated ransomware burst characteristic of this family.

ucs.title: [LLM] LockBit affiliate self-propagation — PsExec/SMB admin-share remote service execution of encryptor
ucs.description: Hunts LockBit affiliates pushing the encryptor laterally across reachable hosts using PsExec (psexesvc) over SMB admin shares and remote service creation — the canonical BITWISE SPIDER deployment after credential theft. Detects psexesvc.exe spawning interpreters/payloads under a network logon, tying remote tool transfer to remote service execution.
ucs.splunk:
| tstats `security_content_summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name="psexesvc.exe" OR Processes.process_name="psexesvc.exe") AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process span=5m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| stats values(process) as commands values(process_name) as children min(firstTime) as firstTime max(lastTime) as lastTime by dest user parent_process_name
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
ucs.kql:
let RemoteExec = DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "psexesvc.exe" or FileName =~ "psexesvc.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe") or FileName endswith ".exe"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ParentTool=InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256;
let NetLogon = DeviceLogonEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where LogonType in ("Network","RemoteInteractive")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project LogonTime=Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, RemoteIP, RemoteDeviceName;
RemoteExec
| join kind=inner NetLogon on DeviceName, AccountName
| where Timestamp between (LogonTime .. LogonTime + 10m)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, RemoteIP, RemoteDeviceName, ParentTool, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
let RemoteExec = SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has "psexesvc.exe" or NewProcessName has "psexesvc.exe"
| where NewProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine;
let NetLogon = SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4624 and LogonType in (3, 10)
| where TargetUserName !endswith "$"
| project LogonTime=TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName=TargetUserName, IpAddress;
RemoteExec
| join kind=inner NetLogon on Computer, SubjectUserName
| where TimeGenerated between (LogonTime .. LogonTime + 10m)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, IpAddress, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: PsExec Service (psexesvc) Spawning Command Interpreter
id: 4d2b8e1f-3a6c-4e9b-bc7d-2e9f1a4b6c8e
status: experimental
description: Detects psexesvc.exe (PsExec remote service) spawning a command interpreter or scripting host, a hallmark of LockBit affiliate lateral deployment over SMB admin shares.
references:
  - https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa23-165a
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\psexesvc.exe'
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
      - '\regsvr32.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Sanctioned IT administration using PsExec for remote scripting
level: high
tags:
  - attack.lateral_movement
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1021.002
  - attack.t1569.002
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\psexesvc.exe OR *\PSEXESVC.exe OR *\PSEXESVC.EXE) @Image:(*\cmd.exe OR *\CMD.EXE OR *\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\rundll32.exe OR *\RUNDLL32.EXE OR *\regsvr32.exe OR *\RegSvr32.exe OR *\wscript.exe OR *\cscript.exe)
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/psexesvc\.exe/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|rundll32|regsvr32|wscript|cscript)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName], function=[collect([ImageFileName, CommandLine]), count(as=childCount), min(_time, as=firstTime), max(_time, as=lastTime)])
ucs.rationale: After LSASS credential theft, LockBit affiliates (BITWISE SPIDER) characteristically fan the encryptor out to every reachable host using PsExec over ADMIN$/IPC$ and a remote service, rather than dropping it host-by-host. Correlating psexesvc-spawned interpreters with a network/RDP logon in a tight window isolates attacker-driven remote deployment from interactive local admin activity and from beni
